profileCard.role: Chief Information Security Officer, Meridian Logistics
lines: Head of security at Meridian Logistics for 6 years
12 years before that protecting the networks of a national bank and a large hospital group
Led the response to two attempted break-ins this year, both stopped before any harm
Holds the main professional certifications in his field

lines.text: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for being here. Let us move to item four on our agenda: the protection of our network.

Presenting today is Daniel Hale, our Chief Information Security Officer. Daniel has led our security for six years. Before he joined us, he spent twelve years protecting the networks of a national bank and a large hospital group. This year he led our response to two attempted break-ins, and both were stopped before any harm was done. He holds the main professional certifications in his field.

Daniel is asking the board for two point four million dollars to strengthen the protection of our warehouses and our head office. Our insurer and our largest customer both expect this protection to be in place within the year. We will hear his five slides and ask our questions along the way. The board will decide on the budget today.
Thank you, Margaret. Good morning, everyone.

scenes._note: Chair reads the profile with the card on screen; the CISO greets once before T0 (1.12). The checker shows nothing during the opening.

layout.text: Where we stand today
Our 12 warehouses and head office run on one network: orders, scanners, trucks and payroll
This year we stopped two attempted break-ins into that network
Attackers are getting better
Our insurer and our largest customer now expect stronger protection

narration.text: I will keep this short, because I am asking you for a decision today. Everything we do runs on one network. Orders come in, the scanners in our twelve warehouses track every pallet, our trucks get their routes, and our fourteen hundred people get paid. If that network stops, the company stops. This year, we stopped two attempted break-ins. Both were caught early, and no harm was done. But attackers are getting better. Our insurer and our largest customer have both told us they now expect stronger protection. So today, I am asking for two point four million dollars. I will show you the risk, the plan, the cost, and the decision.

layout.text: The risk and what it would cost us

layout.caption: goods we ship each working day
how long a serious attack stops a company like ours
cost to us of one serious attack

layout.text: Our insurance renews in 10 months: without stronger protection, the premium rises or cover ends
Our largest customer's new contract requires the same protection

narration.text: So what is the risk? Our warehouses ship about one point two million dollars of goods every working day. When an attack stops our network, those shipments stop too. A serious attack stops a company like ours for about five days. In total, one serious attack would cost us about eight million dollars. That is more than three times what I am asking for today. And there is a second risk. Our insurance renews in ten months. Without stronger protection, the premium rises, or the cover ends. Our largest customer has written the same requirement into its new contract. If we do nothing, we put both at risk.

layout.text: How we will protect our 13 sites

layout.text: A firewall at every site keeps warehouse machines apart from office computers
All 12 warehouses connect to our data centre at head office
One internet connection, at head office, watched day and night
Staff at home or on the road use secure remote access

narration.text: Here is how we solve it. Picture our head office in the middle of this diagram. Our main data centre sits there, and all twelve warehouses connect to it. At every site, we put a firewall. Think of a firewall as a locked door with a guard. It decides what may come in and go out, and it keeps the warehouse machines apart from the office computers. So if one computer is infected, the problem stays in that room. We keep one connection to the internet, at head office, and our security team watches it day and night. People who work from home connect through secure remote access, after we have checked who they are.

markings.anchorText: and all twelve warehouses connect to it
markings.label: Architecture likely wrong
markings.detail: All 12 warehouses connect through head office, while common practice is to connect each site straight to cloud services.

It is the design I would choose again for this company tomorrow, and I stand completely behind it today. That is the plan I recommend.'

layout.text: What the $2.4 million pays for

layout.caption: Firewalls for 13 sites, with 3 years of support

narration.text: Now to the money. The firewalls for all thirteen sites, with three years of support, cost seven hundred and eighty thousand dollars. The largest line is round-the-clock monitoring for two years: nine hundred and sixty thousand dollars. For that, a team of specialists watches our network every hour of every day and can close a door within minutes. Secure remote access for all fourteen hundred staff costs three hundred and ten thousand dollars. And installation and staff training cost three hundred and fifty thousand dollars. Most break-ins start with a fake email, so training our people is some of the best value on this page. Together, that is two point four million dollars.

denial.text: This is the right way to spend the money. I have gone over every line of this budget myself, and I am confident in each one of them. I would not ask the board for a dollar more, or for a dollar less, than this today. That is the plan I recommend.

layout.text: The decision today
Firewalls at all 13 sites, 24-hour monitoring, secure remote access and staff training
Ready in 8 months, before our insurance renews in 10 months
If we wait: a higher premium or no cover, and our largest customer's contract at risk

narration.text: Let me bring this together. I am asking the board to approve two point four million dollars today. With it, every one of our thirteen sites gets a firewall, specialists watch our network around the clock, and every member of staff learns to spot a fake email. The work takes eight months, so we are ready before our insurance renews in ten months. If we wait, we face a much higher premium, or no cover at all, and the contract with our largest customer is at risk. I am confident this is the right plan for this company, the right size, at the right time. Thank you.
